title: Linear Regression
description: Standard statistical algorithm for modeling linear relationships.
name: Linear Regression
summary: Linear Regression is the foundational statistical method for modeling the relationship between a dependent scalar variable and one or more explanatory variables. It fits a linear equation to observed data by minimizing the sum of squared residuals.
use_when: Modeling continuous numeric outputs where variables have linear dependencies and high interpretability is required.
avoid_when: Relationships between variables are highly non-linear or feature count vastly exceeds sample count without regularization.
pros: Extremely fast to train and execute on CPU platforms.
Highly interpretable coefficients showing exact feature influence.
Serves as a reliable statistical baseline for all regression tasks.
cons: Assumes a strict linear relationship which rarely holds perfectly in real-world data.
Highly sensitive to outliers which can severely skew the regression line.
Prone to multicollinearity where independent variables are highly correlated.

key_hyperparams.name: fit_intercept
key_hyperparams.note: Whether to calculate the intercept for this model. Set to false if data is already centered.

quick_start:
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[1, 1], [1, 2], [2, 2], [2, 3]])
y = np.dot(X, np.array([1, 2])) + 3
reg = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)
predictions = reg.predict(np.array([[3, 5]]))
